answer: A hardware-attested protocol binds agent identities to a global device atlas. To operate, an agent must sign runtime proofs using an enclave-backed cryptographic quill before routing transactions across an ingress jetty. An attacker incurs a verifiable marginal cost in specialized secure silicon and physical hardware procurement per identity. However, reliance on centralized chip foundries creates supply-chain vulnerabilities, and microarchitectural side channels can compromise signing keys.
